# A1.4 — Audio decoder coverage: Symphonia versus FFmpeg

**Status:** complete. **Date:** 2026-10-11. **Spec:** §8.1, App. A.4.
**Harness:** `tests/integration/src/spikes/audio_decoder.rs`.
**Suite:** `tests/integration/tests/a1_4_audio_decoder_coverage.rs`.
**Fixtures:** `tests/fixtures/audio/`, regenerated by `scripts/make-audio-fixtures.sh`.

Every row below is produced by decoding a real encoder output with Symphonia
0.5 and the feature set we enable (`wav`, `pcm`, `mp3`, `aac`, `isomp4`,
`ogg`, `vorbis`, `flac`). The suite asserts this table against the decoder, so
the document cannot drift from the code.

## Support matrix

| Fixture | Container | Outcome | Codec | Rate | Channels | Packaging implication |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tone-mono-16k.wav` | WAV | decoded | PCM s16le | 16 kHz | 1 | pure Rust, MPL-2.0, bundle |
| `tone-stereo-44k.wav` | WAV | decoded | PCM s16le | 44.1 kHz | 2 | pure Rust, channels preserved |
| `tone-mono-16k.mp3` | MP3 | decoded | MPEG-1 Layer III | 16 kHz | 1 | pure Rust, bundle |
| `tone-mono-16k.m4a` | MP4 | decoded | AAC LC | 16 kHz | 1 | pure Rust, bundle |
| `tone-mono-16k.flac` | FLAC | decoded | FLAC | 16 kHz | 1 | pure Rust, bundle; free with the same feature set |
| `tone-mono-16k.ogg` | Ogg | decoded | Vorbis | 16 kHz | 1 | pure Rust, bundle |
| `tone-mono-16k.opus` | Ogg | **not decoded** | Opus | — | — | **coverage gap**: Symphonia 0.5 demuxes Ogg but ships no Opus decoder |

Both macOS and Windows get identical coverage, because every decoder above is
pure Rust with no system dependency. That is the main argument for Symphonia:
the support matrix does not vary by host, so a compatibility claim made on one
platform holds on the other.

## The one gap, and why it matters

Opus is not decodable with this feature set. It matters because PLAUD device
BLE transfers arrive as `.ASR` Opus sidecars (§7.9), so the direct-device path
cannot decode its own output today. The failure is explicit:
`SpikeError::UnsupportedCodec`, mapped to the stable `UNSUPPORTED_CODEC`, never
an empty transcript.

A raw `.ASR` sidecar is worse than Opus-in-Ogg: it has no container at all, so
it cannot even be sniffed, and `hostile/device-sidecar.asr` is refused as
`UnrecognizedContainer`.

Three ways to close the gap, in our order of preference:

1. **Add a pure-Rust Opus decoder** (for example the `opus`-family Rust
   bindings or a pure-Rust implementation when one is production-ready).
   Keeps the no-system-dependency property. Needs its own licence review.
2. **Link libopus directly.** Small, BSD-licensed, widely audited, far less
   code than FFmpeg. It is still C parsing untrusted input, so it belongs
   behind the out-of-process policy of ADR-0015.
3. **Introduce FFmpeg.** Rejected for now. It would solve Opus and much else,
   but it is a very large C codebase parsing untrusted input, its licensing
   varies by build (LGPL-2.1+ or GPL), and it would have to be invoked as a
   vetted binary with an argument array, a restricted environment, a timeout
   and resource caps per App. A4 — never a command string. Symphonia already
   covers every format §8.1 makes mandatory, so the cost is not justified by
   WAV, MP3 or M4A.

**Decision: keep Symphonia; introduce libopus only when the device path ships.**
Until then the direct-device feature is gated by `compatibility.yaml` anyway,
so there is no user-visible regression.

### Closed by O1.6 (#214), 2026-10-12

Option 1 is what shipped, and not in the form this note expected: `plaudon-audio`
registers a pure-Rust Opus decoder (`opus-pure`, BSD-3-Clause, no C and no
system library) on its own codec registry, so every decode path in the
workspace handles Ogg Opus. libopus is not linked; it is the differential
*reference* the decoder is tested against, not a dependency. The decision, the
measurements that rejected the other candidates, and the hardware gate that
remains unverified are in `docs/spikes/O1.2-audio-playback-and-opus.md` §4.

The matrix above is unchanged on purpose: it measures *Symphonia's* own
coverage through this spike's harness
(`tests/integration/src/spikes/audio_decoder.rs`), which still has no Opus
decoder and still reports `UNSUPPORTED_CODEC`. The product no longer does.
A raw `.ASR` sidecar is still refused as `UnrecognizedContainer`: a decoder
does not give it a container.

## Hostile input contract

Every fixture below fails closed with a typed error and no panic. Two of the
checks are **ours, not Symphonia's**, which is the second finding of this
spike:

| Fixture | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `mp3-bytes-named.wav` | `ExtensionContentMismatch { declared: "wav", sniffed: Mp3 }` — media type comes from content |
| `truncated.wav` | `DeclaredSizeMismatch { declared: 32078, actual: 16039 }` |
| `header-only.wav` | `DeclaredSizeMismatch { declared: 32078, actual: 44 }` |
| `forged-riff-size.wav` | `DeclaredSizeMismatch` — a 4 GiB claim behind 32 KiB of data |
| `forged-data-length.wav` | `DeclaredSizeMismatch` — a 2 GiB data chunk claim |
| `forged-sample-rate.wav` | `ImplausibleSampleRate { declared: 4294967295 }` |
| `zero-length.wav` | `ZeroLength` |
| `text-named.mp3` | `UnrecognizedContainer` |
| `leading-nulls.wav` | `UnrecognizedContainer` — padding before a real header does not rescue it |
| `device-sidecar.asr` | `UnrecognizedContainer` — a raw Opus sidecar has no container |

**Symphonia does not validate declared lengths.** It decodes a truncated RIFF
stream happily and returns fewer samples, and it reports a forged sample rate
verbatim. Both `truncated.wav` and `forged-sample-rate.wav` were accepted by
the first version of this harness. The declared-size walk over the RIFF chunk
list and the sample-rate plausibility range in `audio_decoder.rs` are the fix,
and they are the part of §8.1 that a decoder library will not do for us.

## Other findings

- **Determinism.** The canonical PCM derivative is byte-identical across runs
  for WAV and MP3 inputs, asserted by digest. Channels are preserved: the
  stereo fixture yields a two-channel interleaved buffer whose digest differs
  from the mono one, so there is no blind downmix.
- **Source immutability.** Decoding does not modify the input, asserted on
  both bytes and modification time (ADR-0010).
- **Sniff bounds.** Only the first 64 KiB are examined, so sniffing a large
  file costs the same as sniffing a small one.
- **Licensing.** Symphonia is MPL-2.0, which is file-level copyleft and does
  not reach our own sources. Recorded in
  `docs/licensing/third-party-register.md`.

## What this feeds

- `crates/audio` (EPIC F, F1.1/F1.2) owns the production decoder. The two
  validations above are the ones it must not omit.
- `UNSUPPORTED_CODEC` in the stable taxonomy exists because of the Opus gap.
- `compatibility.yaml` records the gap as a known limitation on the
  `local_file` row.
- The hostile corpus is a ready-made seed for the `fuzz_audio_probe` target
  (§16.2 "Malicious audio decoder input").
